name: Saadian Tombs
hero_subtitle: A royal burial ground, sealed for two centuries and rediscovered in 1917.

overview.title: A Royal Necropolis Hidden for Centuries
overview.p1: The tombs date back to the 16th-century reign of Sultan Ahmad al-Mansur and hold around 60 members of the Saadian dynasty, plus over a hundred more graves of family members and officials. They were sealed off and forgotten for over two centuries, then rediscovered in 1917 through an aerial survey.
overview.p2: The highlight is the Hall of Twelve Columns, built with Italian Carrara marble and topped with a richly decorated ceiling. The site is small and the entrance passage is narrow, so timing matters more than time: arrive early and you'll enjoy it in peace.

moods.title: What to See at the Saadian Tombs
moods.subtitle: A compact site with three main stops.

1.title: The Hall of Twelve Columns
1.desc: The main mausoleum of Ahmad al-Mansur is the most celebrated room, with marble columns and a gilded, carved ceiling.

2.title: The Garden Cemetery
2.desc: Hundreds of graves of family members and officials lie among trees and low walls, in sharp contrast with the grand mausoleum.

3.title: The Kasbah District
3.desc: The tombs sit beside the Kasbah Mosque, a good starting point for a walk to El Badi and Bahia palaces.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Saadian Tombs

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Enter through the narrow passage beside the Kasbah Mosque on Rue de la Kasbah. A petit taxi will drop you at the top of the street.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Open daily, roughly 9:00 to 17:00. Arrive close to opening time, because the entrance passage gets crowded quickly.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: It is a short visit, so pair it with El Badi Palace and Bahia Palace, all reachable on foot from each other.

q1.question: How long do you need at the Saadian Tombs?
q1.answer: Usually 30 to 45 minutes, plus any time you spend queueing at the entrance.

q2.question: What is the best time to visit the Saadian Tombs?
q2.answer: Right at opening. The site is small and the entrance passage fills quickly with groups.

q3.question: How much is the entrance ticket?
q3.answer: Around 70 MAD. Prices and hours can change, so check locally before you go.

q4.question: Why were the Saadian Tombs forgotten?
q4.answer: They were sealed off and left forgotten for over two centuries, until an aerial survey rediscovered them in 1917.
